Hypercasual Teardown

Paper.io 2

Every percent of land is paid for with a stretch of exposed line. Paper.io 2 turns one finger-drag into a running bet: how far from home dare you draw before someone crosses your trail?

You steer a small cube that never stops. Inside your own colour you are safe; the moment you leave it you drag a pale ribbon that any rival can touch to erase you — and all your land with you. Get back in, and everything the ribbon encloses becomes yours. A loop’s area grows faster than the trail it costs, so the round is a string of decisions about greed, timing and who is nearby.

  • 1–Voodoo · iOS since Aug 2018 · Android shortly after
  • 2–Free to play, ads + in-app purchases
  • 3–App Store 4.5★ from 2.9M ratings (US, 2 Oct 2026)
  • 12–Each round starts at 0.66% of a round arena, one life
01 · The rule

Land is safe, line is not

The whole game is one asymmetry: your territory can’t be hurt by touching it, but the trail you leave outside it is a fuse that anyone can light.

On your landNo trail, nothing to cut. The cube still moves; you choose an exit point.
OutsideA pale ribbon follows the cube. Its length and the time out are your exposure.
Back homeEverything the ribbon encloses fills with your colour; a “+X.XX%” floats up.
Cut / edgeA rival touches your ribbon, or you leave the arena: you shatter and your land vanishes.
Results → againFinal %, kills and a silhouette of what you held; best score persists.

In the recording the opening capture takes about three seconds: the player spawns on the starting disc, swings out into a neighbour’s blue land and comes straight back. The trail turns into territory and a floating +0.13% confirms the gain. Nothing else is taught — the HUD shows the new share, the leaderboard row ticks up, and the next loop starts from a slightly bigger home.

Two details make the rule richer than it sounds. First, the loop does not care whose land it crosses: enclosing a rival’s colour converts it to yours and lowers their share. Second, the “safe” land is safe only from cuts — rivals can still bite pieces of it away with loops of their own, so even an idle player shrinks.

Controls. The official rules say: slide a finger anywhere and the character follows. The cube never stops; the trails in the footage are smooth curves with a finite turning radius, never sharp corners.

Greed geometry: why the next loop is always tempting

Your land (safe from cuts)Your trail (lethal to you if touched)What closing the loop would captureA rival heading for the trail

Illustrative geometry (a semicircular bulge on a straight edge: area = trail² / 2π), not values measured in the game. In the footage, a loop of at least five seconds out returned +1.17% and one of over fifteen seconds returned +1.59% — the clock and the neighbourhood, not geometry alone, decide the real payoff.

02 · The first minute

One tap to play, and the rules arrive as consequences

There is no tutorial in the recorded build. A big yellow Play button drops you on a disc; within fifteen seconds the game has shown a capture, two kills and your own death.

  1. 0 sSpawnDisc at 0.66%, rank 13 of the board; the cube slides out of the disc on its own heading.
  2. +3 sFirst captureLoop through a neighbour’s land: +0.13%.
  3. +7 sFirst killThe trail cuts a rival; it shatters and its whole land disappears; +0.24% on the next return.
  4. +12 sSecond kill“Kill!” floats in the victim’s colour; skull ×2.
  5. +14 sCutA teal rival crosses the long trail; the cube bursts into cubelets.
  6. +15–17 sResults → menu → play1.07%, ×2, best updated; a new colour on the next spawn.

The opening works because the first meaningful input — dragging off the disc — produces the full grammar at once: a trail, a closing loop, a number. The ruleset is then taught by rivals rather than by text. A new player learns cutting by being cut, and learns that the trail is the danger because that is where the cut lands.

The cost is that an early death can feel arbitrary. The rival who ended the first round entered from the edge of the view a second before the cut; in a portrait view the camera shows little of what is approaching the trail. The results card shows what you lost, not why. That gap is the clearest teaching problem for a mobile web version, and the adaptation below addresses it without adding text walls (bridge B10–B11).

The players in the recording are not new: they already knew the game, so first-time understanding is not directly observed. What the footage does show is the speed of the loop — a death to a new controllable round in about three seconds of on-screen time, with likely edits.

03 · Combat

Cutting is the only weapon — and it deletes a whole player

Touch a rival’s trail and that rival is gone at once: the cube bursts, “Kill!” floats up, your skull counter climbs and every square of their land turns back into blank paper.

The kill rewards almost nothing directly — the victim’s land is not transferred to the killer, it simply disappears. What the killer gains is space: open paper next to home that can now be claimed with short, safe loops, and the removal of a threat. In the long round, most kills seen happened at or inside the player’s own border: rivals who loop into your land expose their trails right next to you.

An enemy’s trail stays lethal to its owner even when it runs across your colour. In the long run below, two rivals crossed into the player’s black land with their ribbons and were cut there; one of those kills was the tenth of the round and unlocked the Duck skin on the spot.

Feedback is layered: a burst of small cubes in the victim’s colour at the impact point, “Kill!” tinted in the victim’s territory colour in every kill checked, the skull counter, and — the stable proof — the victim’s land vanishing and their row leaving the board.

04 · Failure and restart

One mistake costs everything you hold

Death is total and immediate: the cube bursts, the land vanishes, and the round is over. What survives is the best score and any skin unlocked along the way.

Three ways out, one of them invisible

  • Cut by a rival. The most common end in the footage. The cause is often off-screen until the last moment.
  • The arena edge. The arena is a large round sheet on a teal background. In the analysed build, driving past its edge ends the run (fig-edge pair). Players still did it — the edge gives no warning beyond the colour change.
  • Your own trail. The official rules say touching your own trail eliminates you; this did not happen on camera, and a 2026 update relaxed it (see Versions).

The results card is the only failure screen: the final share, a dark bar whose meaning the footage does not reveal, the skull count and “Touch to continue”. Touching leads to the menu — sometimes via a “Skin unlocked!” card — and then Play. In the edited footage that loop takes two to three seconds; the decision to try again is never in doubt because nothing is at stake between rounds.

The settled score is what you held at the moment of death, not your peak. In the long run the share fell from 11.16% to 10.56% in the last twelve seconds as two rivals bit into the black land, and 10.56% is what the results card and best score kept.

05 · Territory is never final

Loops steal, and big land is a long border to defend

Any loop that encloses another player’s colour takes it. So the map is not a set of fixed plots but a constant exchange along every border.

Theft makes position matter more than size. A rival’s land next to yours is the cheapest land on the map: a short loop that starts and ends on your border captures it without a long exposed trail. The same logic runs in reverse, which is why big territories erode — every metre of border is a place where someone else can start a cheap loop.

It also explains why the leader is fragile. The crown in the next section sits on the player with the most land, which usually means the longest border and the most rivals within reach of it.

06 · The crown

First place is a visible target, not a reward

The moment your share tops the board, a gold crown appears on your cube. Bots wear it too — and killing whoever wears it is one of the skin dares.

The crown adds no power and no score. It is information: it tells every rival — and the player — who has the most to lose. Because it moves as soon as the lead changes, it also turns the abstract leaderboard into something on the map that can be chased.

For a reconstruction the important properties are the instant transfer (the crown follows rank 1 frame-by-frame), its visibility at the camera’s zoom, and the reward for removing it, which the source ties to a permanent unlock rather than to points.

07 · Meta

Skins are dares that push you into risk

Between rounds there is only one thing to collect: skins. Each is unlocked by doing something risky in a single round — and the conditions read like a list of the game’s best plays.

Unlock condition (as written)SkinWhat it asks of the playerStatus
Kill 10 players in a gameDuckHunt along your border all roundObserved
Kill 50 players in a gamelocked silhouetteAn extreme hunting roundText seen
Cover at least 10% of the mapCow (icon)Grow and surviveObserved
Kill the kingDonutChase the crowned leaderObserved
Stay 5 seconds outside your areagrey animalCommit to a long loopObserved
Stay 10 seconds outside your areapaint-roller cube (icon)A longer loopObserved
Stay 15 seconds outside your areaMouse (icon)Greed under pressureObserved
25 kills; 25/50/80/100% of the map; 3- and 7-day streaksvariousMastery and returnCommunity list

The “stay outside” dares are the most interesting design: they directly reward the exposure that the core rule punishes. In both cases in the footage the unlock banner appeared at the instant the player got home with the loop — never while still outside. Whether the counter needs a safe return or the banner just waits for it is not visible, but either way the dare only pays the player who survives the gamble.

Unlocks are announced by a banner that slides over the top of the HUD for about two seconds; two unlocks earned on one loop queue one after the other. After the round, a “Skin unlocked!” card with an OK button repeats the news, the skin button gets a badge, and the new skin can be selected in a carousel that shows each condition with a progress bar. Skins restyle the cube, the land and the trail — the Donut paints its territory with sprinkles — with no visible gameplay effect.

08 · Interface

A HUD that answers one question: am I growing?

Everything on screen during play is about share and rank. There is no timer, no currency and no button.

The camera follows the cube in a tall portrait view at a fixed zoom in the footage; you see roughly a home-disc’s width either side of you. That is enough to steer, but not enough to see a rival coming for the far end of a long trail — the main readability debt the adaptation has to pay.

09 · Versions

Which Paper.io 2 this is

The analysed mobile recording plays the classic arena: drag to steer, cut to kill, skins by dares. Today’s store build has grown well beyond it, and one supplied recording shows a different web game under the same name.

  • Analysed build (mobile recording; no version string on screen). Round arena, smooth 360° steering, lethal edge, crown, skin dares, menu with an ADS button. This is the model for everything above and for the reconstruction.
  • Current store build (v4.38.1, Sept 2026). Release notes add Heroes with powers fired by double-tap (Dec 2025), countries and a world map, chests, gems, a shop, World League rankings, seasonal events, Party and Team modes, a speed boost for hugging the map edge, and — since v4.32 — the ability to cross your own trail without dying. None of these appear in the analysed footage.
  • Web build (paper-io.com). Square arena with a grey wall, movement on a grid in four directions, square spawn plot, a results page with time played and players killed, and party links. Its geometry belongs to the first Paper.io, so it is used here only as a contrast. The paper-io.com domain now redirects to Voodoo’s Paper.io 2 page.
10 · Product, audience and reception

A mass-market io game sold on immediacy

The store pitch is the loop itself — draw a trail, grow your territory, claim the zone — wrapped in “online multiplayer”, 100+ skins and daily rewards.

The offer today is free with ads and purchases: gem packs from $0.99 to $19.99, No Ads at $9.99 (with a $0.99 trial), a $4.99 skin bundle and other offers; the App Store notes loot boxes and advertising and rates it 9+ (App Store, checked 2 Oct 2026). Google Play lists 100M+ downloads and ads plus in-app purchases (Google Play). Voodoo’s help centre states that the game needs an internet connection (support.paper.io). In the analysed build the menu shows an ADS button; ad breaks themselves are not visible in the edited footage.

Reception snapshot (checked 2 October 2026)

Players · App Store (US)4.5★from 2.9M ratings for the iOS app. Source
Players · Google Play≈4.1★≈2.5M reviews, 100M+ downloads — from search-index snippets and AndroidRank; the Play page itself could not be read in full. AndroidRank
Critics · Metacritic (iOS)1 review148Apps, 60/100 (1 Oct 2018): lag that grows with your territory, luck-dependent spawns and frequent ads. No OpenCritic page found. Metacritic · 148Apps

Steam: the mobile game has no Steam listing; a separate console edition by QubicGames (Switch 2023, Steam May 2024) is a different product and is not rated here. Interpretation: very large store samples with high averages signal broad satisfaction among people who installed it; they say nothing about critics, who largely ignored the game, and they are not sales figures. The single critic review and the Metacritic note agree on one recurring complaint — ads after rounds — which matters for a version that will have none. Sensor Tower placed it #8 among new mobile games worldwide by 2018 downloads and first among US io games in Q4 2023 (2018, Q4 2023).

Audience. The pitch addresses anyone with a thumb and thirty seconds. The design asks for more than it seems: reading rivals’ headings, judging how long a loop can stay out, and accepting total loss many times a minute. The two players in the recording, a child and an adult, play rounds that mostly last seconds and die many times in fifteen minutes; the game still holds them for a long competitive session.

11 · Development & production

A sequel that changed geometry, then kept adding layers

Paper.io (2016) came out of Voodoo’s rapid test-and-iterate publishing; Paper.io 2 (iOS, August 2018) kept the rule and changed the shape of play.

Problem / goalChangeBuild / dateApplies to analysed build?Trade-offSourceTest it implies
Grid movement feels rigid, land looks blocky360° movement, organic territory shapes, round arenaPaper.io 2, 2018YesHarder to judge exact loop geometry148Apps; Game Developer blog (reader post)Curved steering with a finite turn radius (AC-02)
Lag as territory growsNot documentedReview, Oct 2018Unknown—148AppsFrame time stays stable at 25%+ share (AC-19)
Accidental self-cuts“You can now cross your own trail without dying”v4.32.0, 2026No (classic rule in analysed build)Removes a skill check, lowers frustrationRelease notesOwn-trail rule is a declared design choice (R11, AC-07)

Long-term retentionHeroes with powers, countries, chests, gems, World League, eventsDec 2025 → 2026NoPowers change the core duel; currencies add frictionRelease notes; help centreOmitted from the adaptation (bridge B12)

Production principle. The rule that made the game — safe land, lethal line — has never changed. Voodoo changed the geometry once (grid to free curves) and has since layered retention systems around the rule rather than inside it. A small team adapting it should do the same: get the loop’s feel right first, and treat everything else as optional shells.

12 · Takeaways

What transfers

Make the stake physical: the thing you risk should be a line on the map that rivals can see and reach — not a number in a corner.

  • One asymmetry is enough. Safe area vs. exposed line produces greed, timing, ambush and theft without any extra system.
  • Quadratic reward, linear risk. Loops get more valuable faster than they get more dangerous — until a rival notices. That keeps “one more metre” tempting.
  • Kills as space, not loot. Deleting a rival’s land, instead of transferring it, keeps leaders from snowballing and makes every kill a map change.
  • Dares as meta. Unlock conditions that reward the risky play the core punishes give a reason to try specific bold rounds.
  • Pay the readability debt. Fast total failure only feels fair when the cause is visible; the source leaves this to the player, a web version should not.
Build layer

Complete mobile-web adaptation for bug.games

This layer is the single authoritative specification for building the game. Statuses: Observed seen in the inspected footage; Official stated by Voodoo’s help centre or store; Inferred reasoned from several observations; Unknown not established; Designed a decision for the target game, never a claim about the source.

Reading procedure (do this first)
  1. Parse this whole HTML structurally; do not load base64 image data into your text context. Read every collapsed section — all text is in the static file.
  2. Extract every embedded image into your working directory and open each with an image tool. Confirm every ID in the evidence index is present and shows what its row says.
  3. Compare the transitions in the rules against the paired frames (before/after) yourself; captions are summaries, not proof.
  4. Then follow the Build prompt. Keep Observed and Official rules; design the parts listed in design space so they fit the game; record your design choices and test results in your own notes and final report.

Build prompt

Build the complete mobile web game described in this teardown’s Build layer as ONE self-contained, portable HTML file (all code, art, fonts and audio inlined; no network; opens by double-click and runs in a sandboxed iframe on bug.games).

Fantasy: you are a little paper cube who claims a sheet of paper colour by colour. Your land is safe; the trail you draw outside it is your one weak spot.

Keep the core decision (see #b-core, rules R01–R18): leave your land to draw a trail, get back in to capture everything it encloses (rivals’ land included); touching a rival’s trail deletes that rival and all their land; a rival touching yours — or you leaving the round arena — ends your round. The #1 player wears a crown. Score is % of the map; best % persists.

Form: portrait, one thumb, drag anywhere to steer a cube that never stops (#b-loop-input). Rounds are endless free-for-all against 12–16 bots with distinct personalities, one life per round, restart in one tap. Long-term loop: best score plus the full set of skin dares (#b-game, R20) that restyle cube, land and trail; reaching 100% gets a proper celebration.

Design the parts left open (#b-design-space) so they fit this rule set; make the first 20 minutes hook like the best Roblox games using #roblox-hooks and the first-session checkpoints; apply the bridge (#b-bridge) and art direction (#b-art). Improve on the source: show what a loop would earn, why you died and who is coming, while keeping the fast, total-loss tension. Include Settings with English/Russian and separate music and sound-effect volume sliders (#b-settings), and the bug.games integration with no shop at launch unless an extra is fully built (#bug-games).

Deliver the whole game in this build — not a demo or first slice — then play-test on a phone-sized viewport with touch, fix what you find, and report your design decisions and actual test coverage against the expected cases (#b-cases).

Principles (interpretation of the footage, for design guidance). The game creates situations through proximity — every rival’s trail is a target and every border a front. It teaches by consequence (first capture in seconds, first death soon after). It escalates through the player’s own greed and growth: more land means a longer border and a crown that draws attention. It rewards with space (kills free up paper) and with dares that celebrate bold play. Keep all four.

Core statements (must hold in the adaptation)
  1. C1 — Exposure is the price of growth. The player decides where and how far to leave their land; every moment outside adds a trail that can end the round, and closing it converts the enclosed area into land (R03–R05, fig-capture pair, fig-hero/fig-return-unlock).
  2. C2 — Cutting deletes. The player decides whether to chase a rival’s exposed trail; touching it removes that rival and all their land, opening space for safe growth (R06–R07, fig-victim pair).
  3. C3 — Loss is total, retry is instant. A cut or the edge ends the round and erases the land; the next round starts in seconds with only best score and unlocks kept (R08, R10, R13–R15).
  4. C4 — Leading makes you a target. The #1 player is crowned on the map; removing the crown is a goal for others (R17–R18).

Entities and values

  • Spawn share 0.66% (3 spawns). If disc and arena are both circles, disc radius ≈ 0.081 × arena radius (√0.0066) Inf.
  • Loop payoffs seen: +0.13%, +0.24%, +0.23%, +0.17%, +0.22%, +0.28%, +0.31%; ≥5 s outside → +1.17%; ≥15 s outside → +1.59%.
  • Long round: 0.66% → 3.51% (×6) → 5.85% (×9→×10) → 7.56% crown → 10.01% (10% dare) → 11.16% → 10.56% final, ×15 kills, ≈6 min 42 s.
  • Leaders seen on boards: 6–11.7% for bots; ranks down to 14th visible.
  • Opening round: spawn → first capture ≈3 s → kills at ≈7 s and ≈12 s → death ≈14 s; on-screen death → new controllable round ≈3 s (edited footage).
  • Skin names seen: Duck, Cow (icon), Donut, grey animal (5 s), paint-roller cube (10 s), Mouse (15 s). Bot skins seen: taxi, road-trail car, patterned lands.

Art direction and essential signals

Style thesis Des: keep the source’s toy-paper look — flat saturated land slabs with a darker underside, pale trails, small cubes with names — and make it crisper for a phone: higher contrast between land and trail tints, thicker trails, a clearly visible arena edge, and one accent (gold) reserved for the crown and rewards. Camera in portrait: the cube sits slightly below centre so more space ahead is visible; the HUD stays in the top 15% of the screen; the thumb works below the cube; pop-ups float above the cube, never under the thumb.

#SignalFunctionSource figureTarget treatment
S1Own land vs. rival landOwner of every areafig-theft-afterDistinct colours (colour-blind-safe set); slab underside
S2TrailWhere you are vulnerablefig-trail-outLighter tint, rounded, slightly thicker; pulses when a rival head is near
S3CaptureResult of closingfig-capture-afterQuick fill sweep + “+X%” float
S4KillResult of cuttingfig-killBurst in victim colour, “Kill!”, land fade-out in ~0.3 s
S5Danger: edgeWarn before failurefig-edge-beforeGlowing warning band (B5)
S6CrownLeader on the mapfig-crown-afterGold crown readable at phone zoom
S7Off-screen threatWho is coming for your traildonor: Hole.io fig-start-2023Edge arrow + name in rival colour; max 3; only while you have a trail. Borrowed from the indie library (Hole.io teardown, observed 2023 build); not copied: Hole.io’s art.
S8UnlockDare completedfig-unlock-10pctTop banner, queued, never covering the cube

Any third-party file must have a licence that allows commercial use and modification; credits go inside the game HTML. The source game’s art, sounds and the evidence frames are references only.

Game sound in the recording was not listened to and is mixed under commentary and added music. The cues below are designed to serve the observed events.

Settings: languages and volume (target requirement)
  • Des A small Settings entry (gear) reachable from the menu and pause, not shown as a first-run obstacle.
  • English / Russian switch; every player-facing string translated (menu, hints, HUD labels, results, cause lines, dares, banners, errors, platform/extra states). Language can be switched during a paused round and applies immediately.
  • Two independent touch sliders: Music and Sound effects, 0–100%. At 0 the channel is truly silent; moving one never changes the other.
  • Language and both levels saved as device preferences (guarded storage; game still runs if storage is blocked).
bug.games plan: analytics, moments, extras

Des The game is one self-contained index.html. It tries to import /sdk/bloomplay.js from its own origin inside a guarded dynamic import; absence of the SDK (file://, other hosts) and an init error are told apart and both leave the full game playable. Check the current sdk_docs before wiring. Call gameplayStart() when a round becomes controllable and gameplayStop() on death, pause, or leaving to the menu.

Roblox analogs and first-minutes hooks

Knowledge base: Bloom Brain via the search_kb tool and the local clone (~/.bloom-brain/knowledge, 616 pages, snapshot 2026-10-02). Named problems: P1 unclear first action / first loop; P2 the stake is invisible while outside; P3 death without a visible cause; P4 no pull to the next round. Queries: territory capture io trail risk greed crown; push-your-luck unbanked carry bank; FTUE first 30 s first action; death screen cause quick retry; bounty on leader / king; short round best score skins; carried value unbanked deposit indicator. All techniques are Designed, never override R01–R25, and add no currency or monetization.

HookProblemAnalog technique (path, date)Transfer hereRisk to coreHypothesis and test
H1P1Bake or Die — the first task is lit by arrows, no tutorial text (artifacts/pages/bake-or-die-teardown.md, 2026-08-18)First round only: a faint dotted “ghost loop” from the cube out and back to the disc; disappears after the first captureHand-holding the core decisionBefore: first capture depends on luck. After: ≥80% of new testers capture within 10 s (AC-17)
H2P2Steal A Brainrot Egg — carried egg shows “Carrying / Drop” and its cash value ($225) while vulnerable (artifacts/pages/steal-a-brainrot-egg.md, EV012, 2026-09-07); Steal Fish Eggs — the Safe Zone converts the carried egg at a clear boundary (artifacts/pages/steal-fish-eggs.md, 2026-09-08)While outside, a small “+~X%” chip near the cube estimates what closing now would capture; home border glowsPlayers play safer; the chip must not reveal enemy intentTesters can say what they are risking; loop length distribution does not collapse to tiny loops (capture events)
H3P3Infected Lands — death screen states cause, survived time and kills (artifacts/pages/infected-lands-gold-candidate-teardown.md, 2026-09-01)Results card adds one cause line (“Cut by Freak”, “Left the arena”, “Crossed your own trail”), time alive and kills; the dimmed world shows the killerSlower retry≥80% of testers name the cause of their last death correctly (AC-08)
H4P4Endless Barkery — Game Over compares current and previous best with an immediate route into another run (artifacts/pages/teardown-endless-barkery-expanded-reconstruction-brief.md, 2026-09-15)Results card shows “10.56% · best 10.56% NEW” and the nearest dare progress (“Kills in a round 6/10”); one big AgainTurns rounds into a grindMedian results-to-Again <3 s; more rounds per session than without the card (A/B in dev)

Considered and not used: bounty/king economies (Jailbreak, Agartha Mog or Die) — they need currency, and the source already has the crown and Kill the king; cosmetic currencies and battle passes (DOORS, Rivals) — not in the source and not requested.

Open questions and readiness
  • Head-on rule, own-trail behaviour on camera, arena size, speed, turn rate, bot logic, spawn rules and the meaning of the results bar are not established → design space DS-1…DS-10.
  • First-time onboarding was not recorded (experienced players). Ads are not visible in the edited footage.
  • Game audio was not heard; the audio brief is designed.
  • Readiness: complete-game specification ready with named limits; package delivered as this single HTML. Fidelity of a future build must be tested separately (cases above).
